Building & Renovating

Green Building Residential Non-Residential Sign Permits Secondary Suites Agricultural

Delta's Building/Plumbing Bylaw applies to all construction, alteration, reconstruction, demolition, removal, relocation and occupancy of all new and existing buildings and structures. What you need to know:

  • Applications for permits are reviewed for compliance with Delta's bylaws and provincial codes.
  • On-site inspections are conducted to ensure the work is being done correctly and in accordance with the building permit.
  • Successful completion of building and plumbing permits results in the building receiving an occupancy permit.
  • This building permit becomes part of the permanent record in the property file. This information is important to future property owners since it assures them that the work was done in accordance with applicable zoning, health and life-safety regulations.
  • Permits may be required prior to work and a variety of the permits below may be required as part of your project.

Building Permits

Not sure if you need a building permit? See the lists below.

When in doubt, please discuss your project with the Building Division by Contacting the Application Centre at 604-946-3380 or development@delta.ca. Please note that guidance is based solely on the information provided. Different or additional information could possibly result in a different response.

  • A building permit is required to do any of the following:

    • Construct a new principal building;
    • Construct a new accessory building (including a coach house or garden suite)
      • Note: One accessory building with a floor area less than 10 m2 (107.6 ft2) does not require a permit, unless it contains operating mechanical equipment. However, the location must conform to Delta's zoning requirements.  
    • Add to an existing building
    • Alter, renovate or repair existing buildings or structures
    • Repair fire damaged buildings or structures
    • Complete an unfinished area in an existing building; e.g.: basement
    • Construct a secondary suite
    • Move a building from one location to another
    • Demolish or relocate buildings
    • Construct inground swimming pools, hot tubs, or fishpond that are equal to or greater than 450 mm (17.7 in) in depth
    • Construct a retaining wall equal to or greater than 1.2 m (3 ft 11 in) in height 
    • Construct retaining wall on designated steep slope properties regardless of height
    • Install a chimney

     

    See clarification/exceptions provided in list below.

  • A building permit is not required for minor modifications such as: 

    • Cupboards
    • Planters
    • Partial height room dividers
    • Painting
    • Landscaping, including patios and decks less than 600 mm (1 ft 11 in) above grade
    • Sidewalks and driveways
    • Fences (fence height must comply with intersection sightline requirements and Delta's Zoning Bylaw)
    • Roofing repair or replacement
    • Exterior finish repair or replacement; e.g.; siding or stucco;
      • Note: Although the above exterior finish repair or replacement does not require a building permits, owners are responsible to ensure that the work conforms to the requirements of the BC Building Code and Delta Zoning Bylaw.

  • The building permit application requirements depend on the nature and scope of the proposed work. See the Residential, Non-Residential and Secondary Suite pages for the submission requirements for common types of construction and renovation projects. For unique projects, contact the Application Centre at development@delta.ca or 604-946-3380 to confirm the submission requirements.

  • Building permit fees include a Plan Processing Fee (payable at time of application) and a Building Permit Fee (payable at time of building permit issuance). See the link for current fees.

  • Following building permit issuance, inspections are required before, during and after construction to ensure the work has been completed in accordance with the approved plans. Inspections can be requested online up to five days in advance using eInspections, and can be cancelled or rescheduled up until 8 am on the day of the inspection. See our Guide for Scheduling Inspections Online and the list of required inspections.

  • Eligible residential developments can receive a rebate on building permit fees and the heritage conservation levy as of May 6, 2025. This is a temporary program, and funding is available while supplies last. See City of Delta Bylaw No. 8515 for full program details. Contact Community Planning (Development Department) at development@delta.ca or 604-946-3380 to learn if your development may be eligible.

Plumbing Permits

  • A plumbing permit is required when you install, alter or repair plumbing, including for on-site hydrant and service lines (water, sanitary and/or sewer).

  • In addition to the application forms required for all plumbing permit applications, for non-single detached residential dwellings isometric drawings and a plumbing fee calculation form are required. See the How to Apply for application forms which list the submission requirements.

    Please note that all inside plumbing work must be done by a plumber holding a trades qualification and a current City of Delta Business Licence, in compliance with the BC Plumbing Code, except in the case of an owner/occupier of a single detached residential dwelling, who personally does the work, and signs a declaration.

  • The plumbing permit fees are calculated based on the number of fixtures and whether the work involves installation of a fire sprinkler system, hydrants or other fire connections, and/or hot water heating systems. See the link for current fees.

  • Following plumbing permit issuance, inspections are required before, during and after construction to ensure the work has been completed in accordance with the approved plans. Inspections can be requested online up to five days in advance using eInspections, and can be cancelled or rescheduled up until 8 am on the day of the inspection. See our Guide for Scheduling Inspections Online and the list of required inspections.

Demolition Permits

  • A demolition (or decommission) permit is required when you demolish or remove:

    • a building or structure that is larger than 10 m2 in building area and taller than 600 mm 
    • a swimming pool, hot tub, or fish pond deeper than 450 mm
    • a retaining wall exceeding 1.2 m in height
    • a secondary suite
    • a porch, sundeck, carport or garage
    • interior walls

  • Please see the How to Apply (Demolition Permits section) for application forms which list the submission requirements.

  • The demolition permit fee is $153.

  • Following demolition permit issuance, inspections are required before, during and after demolition. Inspections can be requested online up to five days in advance using eInspections, and can be cancelled or rescheduled up until 8 am on the day of the inspection. See our Guide for Scheduling Inspections Online.

    Please note that demolition cannot take place until inspections have been passed for tree protection and capping of services.

Gas and Electrical

Administration of safety standards and safe installation of electrical systems, gas, boiler and other technical equipment in British Columbia is delegated to Technical Safety BC. For more information and to learn more about compliance standards, contact Technical Safety BC.

  • A permit is required to install or alter gas lines. For gas and propane permit information, contact Technical Safety BC.

    At the time of framing inspection for non-complex building permits, the City of Delta requires contractors/builders to provide the Building Inspector with documentation verifying that gas permit(s) have been issued by Technical Safety BC.

  • A permit is required to install or alter electrical wiring or fixtures. For electrical and boiler permit information, contact Technical Safety BC.

    At time of framing inspection for non-complex building permits, the City of Delta requires contractors/builders to provide the Building Inspector with documentation verifying that electrical permit(s) have been issued by Technical Safety BC.

Building Permit Statistics

The City of Delta makes no representation or warranty, express or implied, in respect of the accuracy, completeness or currency of the information. All information pertaining to building permits must be confirmed directly with the Community Planning and Development Department. The City of Delta shall not be liable for any damage whatsoever arising from any use of or reliance on any information included in or excluded from the list.
